presentations.label: presentation studies
presentations.definition: formats for reading, arranging and comparing case material.

concepts.label: game concepts
concepts.definition: proposals for the player’s activity, objectives and progression.

playables.label: playable scenarios
playables.definition: implemented situations with fixed rules, resources and outcomes.

tools.label: design tools
tools.definition: applications for composing scenes, editing relationships and testing rules.

agency.label: agency models
agency.definition: limits on what the player knows, controls and can change.

implementationStates.outlined: central activity identified; detailed rules remain open.
implementationStates.specified: rules or structure described; a complete runtime is not available.
implementationStates.implemented: an interactive artifact exists; its scope is stated separately.

entries.title: forensic explainer
entries.lead: a chaptered case account organized as diagrams, tables and records.
entries.question: can readers trace an explanation to its supporting records?
entries.limit: presentation only; no management economy or player-controlled outcome.

entries.title: specimen world + component bench
entries.lead: case material arranged as draggable paper, terminals and interactive specimens, with a separate component inspector.
entries.question: which document interactions make dense information easier to examine?
entries.limit: visual interactions and calculations; no production schedule or management economy.

media.caption: paper, terminal and component formats · schematic

entries.title: agency as a park
entries.lead: an agency represented as a park: departments, client and supplier visitors, sites and placeable work.
entries.question: which objects require placement, and which belong in a record view?
entries.limit: the placement model must distinguish projects, sites and legal entities.

entries.title: operating campus
entries.lead: run a fictional agency through staffing, production, suppliers and commitments. investigate problems when they affect delivery.
entries.question: does routine management sustain attention before an investigation begins?
entries.limit: the portfolio, department and facility systems exceed the scope of the current scenarios.

media.caption: workshop activity · 8-second illustration; episode state held

entries.title: reconstruction park
entries.lead: arrange a reconstruction, compare records and test which explanations the evidence supports.
entries.question: does comparing evidence create meaningful choices?
entries.limit: a standalone reconstruction scenario is not available.

entries.title: operating game + historical anchors
entries.lead: combine fictional management chapters with short comparisons against fixed historical records. deeper case reading is optional.
entries.question: does the historical comparison improve understanding of the preceding run?
entries.limit: the complete campaign and historical interactions are unbuilt.

media.caption: management chapters and historical comparisons · schematic

entries.title: 28-quarter chronology campaign
entries.lead: a 28-quarter campaign with dated unlocks, relationship tests and progression after each required relationship is mapped.
entries.question: does timeline progression support discovery or only delay access?
entries.limit: the campaign runtime is unavailable. the prototype 2 runtime contains the shorter make/buy scenario.

entries.title: prototype 2 · make or buy
entries.lead: choose between shared shop capacity and supplier cash. run each plan, inspect the tradeoff and revise. both plans can deliver.
entries.question: can players understand and replay the capacity–cash tradeoff without guidance?
entries.limit: a short staged scenario; no half-day production calendar.

entries.title: ordinary-work-first practice
entries.lead: schedule production through half-day turns, shared staffing and work-bay choices. the supplier payment succeeds.
entries.question: do staffing and placement create useful choices without a payment conflict?
entries.limit: eight half-day intervals; no returned-payment investigation in the default scenario.
entries.scope: staff allocation, bay placement and make/buy choice

entries.title: episode 01 · the handoff

facts.main question: delivery decisions under a payment conflict

entries.lead: complete a production job while resolving a returned payment. request records, obtain approval, reissue payment or arrange substitute production.
entries.question: does record inspection change an operating decision?
entries.limit: fictional values and responses. historical comparison is disabled; participant comprehension and session length are unmeasured.
entries.scope: production and payment conflict; ordinary control available

media.caption: returned payment → approval → handoff · condensed playthrough

entries.title: standalone park builder
entries.lead: place, move and remove objects, people and looping events. compose a scene and export a gif.
entries.question: which arrangements improve spatial readability and interaction?
entries.limit: scene composition only; object placement has no financial or production effects.

media.caption: shared park objects · composed animation loop

entries.title: design whiteboard
entries.lead: edit shared records through systems, story and structure views. draw connections, replay scenario rules and save checkpoints.
entries.question: can a group test relationships and assumptions while keeping rules distinct from notes?
entries.limit: shared rooms require a configured supabase project. notes and drawn connections have no effect unless assigned a rule.

media.caption: systems → story → structure · three views of shared records

entries.title: tabletop game
entries.lead: a tabletop alternative to the tycoon format, with monopoly as a reference for board-based play.
entries.question: which shared activity and outcome should the tabletop format support?
entries.limit: player count, actions, ownership rules, turn structure and victory conditions are undefined.

entries.title: bounded historical role
entries.lead: play a role within a historical sequence. available information, authority and local actions are constrained by that role.
entries.question: what could this role know, authorize and change at each point?
entries.limit: permitted actions and their effects are undefined. no historical-role scenario is implemented.

media.caption: bounded agency within fixed history · schematic

entries.title: open counterfactual management
entries.lead: manage a fictionalized situation in which interventions can produce different outcomes.
entries.question: which outcomes should player decisions be able to change?
entries.limit: the extent of control, available interventions and relationship to historical events are undefined.

relationTypes.tests: implements a bounded part of a concept.
relationTypes.supports: provides a design activity for a concept.
relationTypes.uses: loads rules or records from a scenario.

decisions.title: purpose
decisions.definition: the intended effect of the game beyond completing a session.
decisions.question: what should the game help people understand, experience or do?

decisions.title: audience
decisions.definition: the people the game is designed for, including their knowledge and context of play.
decisions.question: who is playing, and what do they already know?

decisions.title: format
decisions.definition: the medium and session structure through which play happens.
decisions.question: which activities need a simulation, a reconstruction interface or a tabletop format?

decisions.title: player role
decisions.definition: the position from which the player receives information and takes action.
decisions.question: is the player an operator, an investigator or a participant in another defined role?

decisions.title: agency
decisions.definition: the information, permissions and outcomes the player can change.
decisions.question: which events remain fixed, and which respond to player decisions?

decisions.title: session outcome
decisions.definition: the conditions that end play and the result presented at closeout.
decisions.question: what constitutes completion, success or failure for the chosen concept?

mechanisms.title: what gets placed?
alternatives: clients, offices and affiliated companies as possible attractions
projects as work clusters; sites, clients and legal entities kept distinct
mechanisms.scope: proposed taxonomy; only small scenarios implemented

mechanisms.title: billpay: kiosk or workbench?
alternatives: a spatial kiosk or a separate mini-game
a record and payment workbench; only physical handoffs use distance

mechanisms.title: one world, several views
alternatives: interactive infographic showing money, information and control
work / cash / information / control / people with retained selection
mechanisms.scope: implemented with different scope in each playable

mechanisms.title: three desk arrangements
alternatives: a 1990s desktop for records and discoveries
world + inspector; compare two records; read with a return target
mechanisms.scope: interface proposal with working record drawers and material studies

mechanisms.title: office-space collection
alternatives: mckibbin, boerum, johnson, porter, colorado and hong kong as a pack
site identity separate from occupancy, department, ownership and obligations
mechanisms.scope: three office-derived buildings developed; full site economy unbuilt

mechanisms.title: small attractions and easter eggs
alternatives: office photographs become landmarks and possible activities
chrysler loop, fedora moonwalk, cat, cutaways, courtyard variants and voila route
mechanisms.scope: scenic interactions; no economic or evidence rewards attached

mechanisms.title: sandbox extensions and mods
alternatives: stable object types, scenario settings and separate source records
mechanisms.scope: data boundaries proposed; no general mod platform built

sources.title: initial design manual
points: operating campus: fictional production and resource management.
reconstruction park: compare records and build a supported explanation.
combined concept: management chapters followed by historical comparisons.

sources.title: initial object model
points: a project coordinates deliverables, labor and supplier requirements.
a site supplies space and facilities. occupancy connects it to an organization over time.
a legal entity holds accounts, contracts, assets and obligations.
a payment attempt has its own settlement state. a record documents a claim about that state.

sources.title: three desk arrangements
points: world + inspector: retain a selected object while showing its records.
comparison: place related records side by side.
reading: open a document with a return point to the prior task.

sources.title: current game proposal
points: the operating concept covers staffing, suppliers, delivery and cash commitments.
the reconstruction concept covers conflicting records and supported explanations.
historical comparison has separate access and evidence requirements.

sources.title: episode 01 implementation
points: the scenario advances in half-day intervals.
production, cash, records and permissions constrain the available responses.
the returned-payment route and ordinary control are separate scenario settings.

sources.title: episode 01 rules
points: opening cash: $40,000.
internal production: six fabrication units, two packing units and $4,000 materials.
supplier commitment: $12,000.
a three-unit display job is due tuesday afternoon. the run permits up to twelve half-day intervals.

sources.title: prototype 2 runtime
points: opening cash: $48,000.
internal plan: twelve of sixteen shop hours and $6,400 modeled cost.
supplier plan: $12,000 reserved; posted cash remains unchanged.
the competing eight-hour job queues four hours under the internal plan.

sources.title: prototype 2 evaluation criteria
points: the core decision is shared capacity versus usable cash.
plan comparison requires a visible consequence for the second job.
the scenario tests whether the tradeoff can be understood and replayed without guidance.

sources.title: earlier campaign integration note
points: the campaign spans twenty-eight quarters.
dated records unlock as the timeline advances.
relationship checks gate progression to the next quarter.
the campaign runtime is unavailable.

sources.title: ordinary-work-first practice
points: two staff units are available per half-day.
internal production requires four fabrication and two packing units, plus $4,000 materials.
the $12,000 supplier route settles successfully.
staff allocation and work-bay placement affect delivery.

sources.title: ordinary practice checks
sources.revision: recorded 17 september 2026; not a participant test
points: model checks cover production, staffing, bay placement and ordinary payment.
automated checks establish runtime behavior. participant comprehension and session length remain unmeasured.

sources.title: whiteboard / cms boundary
points: a record has one identity across systems, story and structure views.
rules, narrative beats, objects and notes are distinct types.
scenario effects are evaluated by the episode rules.
local saves and shared rooms use separate persistence mechanisms.

sources.title: park interaction studies
points: a spatial object represents a site, facility, work cluster or landmark.
physical handoffs can depend on distance.
payment and information relationships need explicit states and permissions.
scenic routes and small animations have no economic effects.

sources.title: published tools and build inventory
points: the design reader presents the current specification.
the episode is a production and payment scenario.
the park builder composes scenes. the whiteboard edits and replays relationships.
the sprite catalogue and preview library provide shared visual assets.

sources.title: existing production sequence
points: p2: test the ordinary production loop without instruction.
p3: compare operating and reconstruction structures.
p4: evaluate the full fictional episode.
purpose, audience and format remain separate design decisions.

sources.title: early forensic explainer plan
points: the presentation organizes a case account into chapters.
diagrams show relationships, timelines and flows.
source records support the explanatory sequence.

sources.title: specimen-world design brief
sources.revision: brief says june 2026 · adjacent presentation work
points: documents become movable paper, terminals and interactive specimens.
a component bench isolates reusable controls and material treatments.
the presentation has no production calendar or management economy.

sources.title: retained design 0.3
points: design 0.3 retains the early operating and reconstruction alternatives.
the retained copy has the same gameplay text as the archived 0.3 specification.

sources.title: systems research proposals
points: projects compete for staff, facilities and supplier capacity.
contracts create commitments before cash movement.
deliveries depend on both production and handoffs.
information and authority restrict which corrective actions are available.

sources.title: design revision history
points: design 0.1–0.16 covers the operating concept, episode rules, art system and authoring tools.
alternate-branch scenarios retain separate schedules and resource values.
revision numbers identify artifacts; they do not define a single gameplay sequence.

sources.title: spatial game model
points: agency-as-park: placeable work and sites, departments as staff, client and supplier visitors.
bill-payment interface: a spatial kiosk or a record workbench.
player agency: bounded actions within history or variable outcomes in a fictionalized scenario.

sources.title: purpose, audience and format
points: purpose defines the intended effect. audience defines who the game serves.
format defines the medium and session structure.
tabletop play is an alternative with undefined mechanics. monopoly is a reference.
player role, agency and session outcomes remain open.
